summary: MURFX is a browser-native astronomical analysis studio that turns NASA SPHEREx’s wide-field infrared cubes into high-precision discoveries. By uniting sub-pixel astrometric centroiding, dipole difference imaging, and multi-mission catalog cross-matching, MURFX empowers both professional astrophysicists and citizen scientists to visually track, measure, and verify ultra-cool brown dwarfs, near-Earth asteroids, and hypothetical Planet X candidates across 6-month survey passes.
details: MURFX is a browser-native astronomical studio that uses sub-pixel centroiding, dual-mode blinking, and dipole difference imaging to track moving brown dwarfs and solar system bodies across NASA SPHEREx’s 102-channel infrared survey passes.It detects sub-pixel motion down to 0.02 pixels0.02\text{ pixels}0.02 pixels (120 mas120\text{ mas}120 mas) on low-resolution detectors, eliminates false alarms caused by molecular absorption dimming, and enables instant multi-wavelength verification with zero software installation.It democratizes deep-space astrophysics by allowing everyday citizen scientists to rapidly screen and validate SPHEREx data releases, accelerating the discovery of cold brown dwarfs, near-Earth asteroids, and hypothetical outer solar system planets.Built with JavaScript (ES Modules), HTML5 Canvas 2D/WebGL, CSS Bento Grid, Web Audio API, and Node.js/FastAPI, integrating live data from NASA SPHEREx/IRSA/AllWISE, ESA Gaia DR3, CDS Aladin Lite/SIMBAD, and CSA NEOSSat.It introduces real-time "dipole difference subtraction" that erases static stars into pitch black to reveal movers, features 1-click discovery bridging directly from the canvas into citizen science logs, and converts 102-channel infrared spectra into audible musical chords.We prioritized strict astrometric mathematical rigor, hardware accessibility so it runs smoothly on any basic laptop, WCAG AA visual/audio inclusivity, and multi-catalog verification to rule out cosmic rays, optical artifacts, and satellite tracks.
